  • Milspec upper and lower, ideally from a custom shop
  • Rainer Ultramatch Mod 2 barrel of your flavor of caliber in .223, 5.56 NATO, 225 Valkyrie, etc
  • Rainer Gas Block
  • Radian Raptor charging handle
  • Geissele DMR HS National Match fire control group
  • Fail Zero NIB 6.8 BCG
  • JP Silent Capture
  • Magpul UBR Gen 2 stock

Optional:

  • Brake (ASR for me, little bastard otherwise)
  • Suppressor (I run ASR's so a Chimera would be ideal)
  • BCM Grip/Foregrip
  • Magpul irons
  • Vortex Prism 3x or EOTECH XPS3
estimated price for your base model and fully loaded?

• Matched 7075-T6 milspec (so forward assist + dust cover + full 0 MOA picatinny) upper/lower runs anywhere from $400-$600 + handguard, so lets say $700 with a floating keymod/picatinny handguard.
  • Barrel varies with price, anywhere from $300 for a 223 Wylde (.223 Rem + 5.56 NATO, best to buy for the standard all-purpose AR-15) to $500 for a 224 Valkyrie long-range precision build.
  • .875 adjustable gas block: $90
  • Radian Raptor charging handle: $90
  • Geissele High-Speed National Match DMR (best trigger group I've ever used for the AR15/AR10): $280
  • FailZero bolt carrier group: $180
  • JP Silent Capture: $75
  • Magpul UBR Gen2: $190
  • Magpul AR-15 MOE+ grip: $20
  • Magpul Pro offset irons (because you are probably going to buy an optic that won't fit co-witness): $160

This is not your off-the-shelf S&W AR-15. This is a fucking Bugatti Veyron and the first time you pull a 3 lb Geissele you will never be able to use another rifle without one again. Entire build would be approximately $2,080 to $2,280 in parts and the only things not included would be a brake ($80-$150), a suppressor ($800-$1,000), a close-range tactical optic ($200-$300), or a long-range precision optic ($800-$1,600), and maybe a foregrip ($20) or tactical light ($150-$200). Plus magazines, because who wouldn't want a Magpul 60-round drum magazine, and a bunch of 30 and 40-round Magpul P-mags?

You can dump another $3,000 into low-weight titanium parts (upper, lower, stock, guard, etc) and reduce the weight of the rifle down to about 1/3rd, too. Fun hobby.
